title: rubric_score excluded from metrics by skill instruction, breaking rolling-average regression detection
description: run.skill.md explicitly instructs agents: 'do NOT compute or write rubric_score' in the metrics file. This means all historical metrics files lack rubric_score. The reviewer's rolling-average regression detection cannot function without this field — there is no baseline to compare against. The exclusion was intentional (avoiding subjective scoring during a run), but the downstream consequence (no regression signal across runs) was not considered at the time the instruction was written.
proposed_resolution:
Option A (preferred): Compute rubric_score as a structured artifact AFTER the QA review, not during the run. Write it to a separate 'review_result' section of the run JSON (not the metrics file) so it is available for the reviewer's cross-run analysis without polluting the run-time metrics.
Option B: Add rubric_score back to metrics, but compute it only in the post-run QA phase and prohibit it from the Phase 3 implementation metrics.
Either way: update the reviewer prompt to read rubric_score from the correct artifact and compute the rolling average for regression detection.
